construction.note: This uses Manuel Martínez Vela’s published grid method and drawing 1 on the eight-pointed-star grid in ALZADA 115, page 45. We read the outlines and supplied the compass construction and step grouping.
construction.changes: The article explains the shared grid and shows the completed tracing. It does not give this pattern’s numbered app sequence. Its separate nine-step Partal example is a different pattern. Source credits identify the design and method, not a verbatim sequence.

credits.source: La Alhambra con regla y compás: el trazado de los diseños geométricos nazaríes (ALZADA 115, 2017)
credits.creator: Manuel Martínez Vela
credits.note: The grid of eight-pointed stars (each turned square found with a circle through the diagonal grid corners) and the tracing of this Comares panel (the article's drawing 1) follow this article.

given.O: The centre of one eight-pointed star.
given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is one square of the grid.

steps.text: Rule a horizontal line through the centre and draw a small circle. Its radius is one square of the grid, and the compass keeps this opening while you build the grid.
Rule the vertical through the centre. Walk the compass along both lines, both ways, marking a point every square.
Through every mark rule a line at right angles to its axis. The lines make a square grid.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Through the first mark on each side of the centre, rule a line at right angles to its axis. The four lines make the square around the centre.

steps.text: Open the compass from the centre to the corner of a square diagonally next to it, and draw that circle: it passes through four grid corners. Where it crosses the horizontal, rule lines at 45° both ways. They form a square standing on its corner, which with the grid square around the centre makes an eight-pointed star.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Open the compass from the centre to the corner of the square, and draw that circle: it passes through its four corners. Where it crosses the horizontal, rule lines at 45° both ways. They form a square standing on its corner, which with the square around the centre makes an eight-pointed star.

steps.text: Mark the crossings where the design turns, and the tile: the square, standing on a corner, whose corners are two squares from the centre along the horizontal and the vertical.

ink.text: Go over the lines of the design. Around the centre they draw an eight-pointed star whose points are notched by the grid; between the stars they close into crosses.

pattern.text: Repeat the tile edge to edge. Notched eight-pointed stars and crosses alternate, as in a tile panel of the Hall of Comares.

expect.note: Golden values in grid squares (OA = one square), computed by the engine; the pieces fill the tile.
